name: neuro-ophthalmology overview
title: Visual symptoms not from the eyeball: double vision sorts by which nerve palsy (third, fourth or sixth), a gaze-evoked nystagmus points to the cerebellum or brainstem, unequal pupils sort by whether the difference is worse in light (parasympathetic) or dark (sympathetic, Horner), and a relative afferent pupillary defect points to one optic nerve; nystagmus is pendular or (mostly) jerk, and the panel below localizes each visual field defect along the visual pathway

root.title: A visual symptom NOT from the eyeball: which kind?
lines: each one localizes to a nerve or a pathway
a missing part of the visual field: see the panel below

groups.title: DOUBLE VISION (diplopia)
lines: lateral rectus = VI · superior oblique = IV · the rest = III

panels.title: Visual field defects: where is the lesion? (left-side lesion shown)
items: NASAL fibres cross at the chiasm, temporal do not · each side of the brain sees the opposite field
optic nerve: vision ↓ in THAT eye only
back of the optic nerve: that eye blind + junctional scotoma (upper temporal) in the other eye
chiasm: BITEMPORAL hemianopia (pituitary macroadenoma from below)
lateral geniculate nucleus: right homonymous sectoranopias (wedges)
temporal lobe (lower radiation): right homonymous SUPERIOR defect
parietal lobe (upper radiation): right homonymous INFERIOR defect
occipital upper bank: inferior quadrantanopia · lower bank: superior quadrantanopia
occipital lobe: right homonymous hemianopia with MACULAR SPARING
tip of the occipital lobe: right homonymous central scotomas
